key_insight: The paper introduces a standardized benchmarking framework that enables fair, repeatable evaluation of neuromorphic controllers on soft robotic platforms, bridging the gap between spiking hardware and embodied intelligence research.
problem_solved: Lack of a common, reproducible benchmark for comparing neuromorphic control strategies on soft robots—making it hard to measure progress, reproduce results, or guide co-design between soft hardware and spiking architectures.
method: Define a suite of embodied tasks and metrics tailored to soft-robotic behaviors (e.g., locomotion, manipulation, energy efficiency, robustness).
Integrate neuromorphic controllers (spiking neural networks) with simulation and physical soft-robot platforms via a reproducible evaluation pipeline.
Provide standardized data formats, evaluation protocols, and comparative visualizations to enable cross-lab benchmarking and hardware/software co-design.
impact: Enables objective comparison and faster iteration on neuromorphic control designs for embodied agents, helping researchers and engineers prioritize architectures and hardware that deliver real-world robotic performance gains.
visual_elements: System schematic: soft robot + neuromorphic chip + simulator + evaluation dashboard showing data flow and integration points.
Example task panel: side-by-side illustrations of benchmark scenarios (locomotion, object manipulation, disturbance recovery).
Performance radar/spider charts comparing controllers across metrics (accuracy, latency, energy, robustness).
Pipeline timeline: steps from controller training → simulation/real deployment → standardized evaluation → leaderboard/results.
paper_title: A benchmarking framework for embodied neuromorphic agents
paper_authors: Giulia D’Angelo, Jens E. Pedersen, Taimoor Hassan, Matteo Cianchetti, Josh Bongard
